reviewed_by: Codex focused review for LAN connection resilience
reason: The branch confirms transient Core health failures before replacing the workspace, preserves the current project route during reconnect, preserves immediate browser-offline handling, classifies response-body aborts as cancellations, and uses origin-neutral startup copy. Seven collected frontend cases cover probe timing, confirmation, recovery, stale responses, and cancellation diagnostics. Thirty-three manifest contract cases validate the new impact mapping. Three catalogued browser journeys verify draft preservation, confirmed loss, and automatic recovery on desktop Chromium, mobile Chromium, and mobile WebKit.
exclusions: Full suites and unrelated backend, provider, harness, terminal, project, native, and desktop-shell workflows are excluded. No Python browser runtime is needed for the manifest contract tests. The selected browser journey uses the production UI bundle with controlled Core responses; authenticated non-loopback real-Core verification remains a separate deployment acceptance step because the fix changes browser connection policy rather than a Core endpoint.
